subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Adders: Adding Numbers in Hardware
description: A micro-lesson that makes Adders: Adding Numbers in Hardware usable.

hook.text: Computers add numbers using gates, not memorized tables. Hardware does the math.

buildup.text: A half adder uses XOR for the sum bit and AND for the carry bit. Two gates, one-bit addition.

discovery.text: A full adder adds three bits — two inputs plus a carry-in — producing sum and carry-out.

twist.text: Chain 64 full adders and you get a 64-bit adder — but the carry ripples through slowly.

climax.text: Carry-lookahead adders predict carries in parallel — trading gates for speed.

punchline.text: XOR for the sum, AND for the carry — addition built from logic gates.

quiz.question: What does a half adder lack that a full adder has?
options: A carry-in input from a previous stage
